newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba ag minister says hog output up on exports.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba ag minister says hog output up on exports.

text.p: Manitoba Agriculture Minister Harry Enns said farmers in this western Canadian province should produce three million slaughter hogs this calendar year, up 20 percent from last year's 2.5 million hogs.

"For 1996 we expect hog output to reach three million. In the last three years we've been expanding at eight to nine percent a year. This Maple Leaf acquisition this morning will maintain that momentum," Enns told Reuters.
Canada's largest food processor, Maple Leaf Foods Inc, bought Burns Foods' hog and beef slaughter plants in Manitoba and Alberta, and its Saskatchewan bacon plant, on Monday.
"This gives confidence to the credit lending agencies to lend money to hog producers and it gives confidence to the feed industry to expand," Enns said.
Manitoba exports 75 to 80 of its hogs. Most are exported to the United States. They also go to Japan, South Korea, and Hong Kong, and may one day go to China, Enns and livestock analysts said.
"On my Asian trips in the last two years I've heard per capita pork consumption is stable but there's a shift in preference to chilled from frozen pork," Enns said.

A Winnipeg consortium's plan to fly 747 cargo freighters carrying consumer goods twice weekly from South Korea and Japan for redistribution throughout North America could haul chilled pork back to Asia Pacific, he said.
"Their backhaul rates come close to matching ocean freight, so you could have chilled Manitoba pork on Tokyo supermarket shelves in 48 hours by plane rather than 10 days by ship," Enns said.
